test_design.transport: ScriptedStreamingTransport implements IPreparedPass2StreamingTransport in-process and records request metadata only.

test_design.callbacks: RecordingRetrievalService provides deterministic accepted/bound-exceeded outcomes, an optional admitted provider projection, and tracks callback order/concurrency. Submission validation is a deterministic local callback.

required_corrections.observed: ReadBoundedAsync timeout cancellation is caught as provider-unavailable because the linked timeout token is not distinguished from provider failure.
required_corrections.expected: Both inactivity and absolute deadline expiry return the closed provider-timeout outcome while preserving zero retry and no raw provider payload.

required_corrections.observed: A shared retrieval callback returns retrieval-bound-exceeded on the restarted run, but the executor ignores the function result and proceeds to accepted submission.
required_corrections.expected: A bound refusal from retrieve_code_logic prevents final acceptance; durable retrieval accounting must remain authoritative across a new executor instance.

required_corrections.vector: canonical transcript and admitted retrieval projection
required_corrections.observed: Request two contains only the original prompt, packet, and declarations; tool-call ID, retrieval handle, and admitted projection are absent, so retrieval output is discarded before the next provider turn.
required_corrections.expected: Every request after tool work carries a bounded canonical transcript with stable tool-call IDs and the actual server-admitted retrieval projection, while preserving the original server context.

required_corrections.observed: A retrieve call with no ID is accepted and the retrieval callback runs eight times as the one scripted response is replayed; the executor returns submission-missing rather than invalid-tool-call before callbacks.
required_corrections.expected: A missing tool-call ID returns invalid-tool-call immediately and invokes zero local callbacks.

required_corrections.observed: Two retrieve calls with the same ID are accepted and callbacks run eight times as the one scripted response is replayed; duplicate IDs are not rejected during whole-batch preflight.
required_corrections.expected: Duplicate IDs return invalid-tool-call before the first callback and make no retrieval or submission mutation.

required_corrections.observed: Request ten is submission-only but repeats the original prompt, packet, and declarations without firstSubmissionCorrection, closed rejection category, deterministic repair code, or server context projection.
required_corrections.expected: Request ten contains only the closed rejection category and repair code plus exact original packet and server-owned retrieval context; raw exceptions, provider content, tool arguments, and reasoning are excluded.

required_corrections.vector: transcript and retrieval-result request byte accounting
required_corrections.observed: A 100,000-byte provider packet plus a 40,000-character admitted retrieval projection still reaches and accepts request two; the projection and transcript are not measured against the 131,072-byte request cap.
required_corrections.expected: The initial request remains under the cap, but the next request is rejected as request-bound before transport when canonical transcript and admitted result bytes would exceed the cap.

required_corrections.vector: early rejected submission skips request nine and uses request ten correction
required_corrections.observed: When the provider submits a candidate on request one and local validation rejects it, the executor sets its loop counter so the next provider submission is request nine. This violates the correction contract by using request nine instead of request ten, even though only two submit callbacks occur.
required_corrections.expected: An early rejected submission must advance directly to the sole request-ten correction, with exactly two provider submit invocations and no request-nine submission or third callback/request.
